ea-gh-the-door.reason: The first two sections answer it (one way into the fold, a Person; every side entrance arrives as a thief); the lesson ends on a sheepfold drawing activity rather than the question.
ea-gh-the-door.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Every spiritual shortcut promises access, so which entrance is real? Only one: Jesus said, I am the door (John 10:9). The way into the Father's fold is a Person, not a technique. Anyone who climbs up some other way may reach something on the other side, but Jesus says they arrive as a thief and a robber (John 10:1). So the question is never only whether something is real. It is which way you came in. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-the-door.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Which way did you come in? There is only one entrance that is real, and it is Jesus, the Door that Yahweh made at the cost of His own Son. Frequencies, rituals, substances and seeking spirits directly are all side entrances that end in stealing, killing and destroying. Through Him you are saved, go in and out, and find pasture. And the Door is open: He will in no wise cast out anyone who comes. You can stop auditing every shortcut and rest. You already know the way in.

teen.open: Lots of things promise a shortcut to the spiritual world. Which way in is real? Only one. Jesus said, I am the door.
teen.close: So skip the shortcuts. Come in through Jesus. He is the only real way in, and He never turns away anyone who comes to Him.

senior.open: The title asks which entrance to the spiritual is real. Jesus answers in John 10: He alone is the Door, and whoever climbs up some other way does so as a thief.
senior.close: So the way we come in matters as much as where we arrive. Through Christ alone we are saved, kept and fed, and having one Door frees us from weighing every new shortcut that is offered.

ea-gh-door-christ.reason: That there is one Door is stated early, but the title's why (only Christ paid the price and opened the way by His Blood) waits for WHY ONLY ONE DOOR mid-lesson; ends on a prompt.
ea-gh-door-christ.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Yahweh's entrance to eternity run through Christ alone? Because only He paid the price that opens it. Jesus said, I am the door, and no man comes to the Father but by Him (John 14:6). No other founder died for the sins of the world and rose again, and the way into Yahweh's presence was opened through His flesh and His Blood (Hebrews 10:19-20). There is no side gate. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-door-christ.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the entrance to eternity run through Christ alone? Because He alone opened it with His Blood, and He states it plainly: one Door, one Name, one Mediator. Like the ark, it has one door, it stands open now, and a day comes when it is shut. Yet it is wide open to anyone, with no background shutting you out. So read His words as He states them, test every path by whether it goes through Him, come in, and find pasture. Now is the day of salvation.

teen.open: Why is Jesus the only way to Yahweh? Because only He died for our sins and rose again. He opened the door with His own Blood.
teen.close: So there's no back door. Jesus is the one Door, and it's open to anyone right now. Come through Him and invite others too.

senior.open: The title asks why the entrance to eternity runs through Christ alone. The Word answers that He alone paid the price that opens it; by His Blood He made the new and living way to the Father.
senior.close: So the one Door is not a human narrowness but the only opening Yahweh made. It stands open to all who come, and love urges people through it while it is still the accepted time.

ea-gh-seek-first.reason: Opening states the promise (seek first, and all these things are added; priority order, not portfolio balance), but the calendar link waits for section eight; ends on a discussion prompt.
ea-gh-seek-first.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What happens when Yahweh's Kingdom comes first? Jesus promises that all these things, food, drink and clothing, shall be added (Matthew 6:33). Provision comes as a byproduct of the right priority, not of anxious chasing, because your heavenly Father knows what you need. The word first is the key: this is priority order, not a balanced portfolio. And your calendar and budget already show which order you are living. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-seek-first.example: WHAT THE CALENDAR SAYS. Say a family looks honestly at last month. Prayer happened when nothing else was scheduled. Giving came from whatever was left after the bills. Worship lost out whenever a game or a shift came up. Nobody decided the Kingdom was last; the calendar simply shows it. Now say they reorder it: the first hour of the day, the first portion of income and the family's worship are set down first, and everything else is planned under them. That is seeking first in ink.
ea-gh-seek-first.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What happens when Yahweh's Kingdom comes first? The anxiety economy is turned upside down. Haggai's people put their own houses first and earned wages into a bag with holes; Solomon asked first for what served the Kingdom and was given riches he never asked for; the widow fed the prophet first and her barrel did not run out. Your calendar and budget are already telling which story you are in. Put the Kingdom on the top line, one day at a time, and all these things shall be added.

teen.open: What happens when you put Yahweh first? Jesus says the things you need get added. Your schedule shows what's really first right now.
teen.close: So look at where your first hour and first money go. Put Yahweh first, trust Him with tomorrow, and He takes care of what you need.

senior.open: The title asks what follows when Yahweh's Kingdom comes first. Matthew 6:33 promises that the needs we would otherwise chase are added, as the fruit of a rightly ordered life.
senior.close: So our calendars and budgets are honest witnesses of our priorities. Ordered with the Kingdom first, day by day, they become the setting in which the Father, who knows our needs, adds what we require.

ea-gh-ask-seek-knock.reason: Section two answers it (keep on asking, seeking, knocking; the asking is the qualifying); delay-is-not-denial comes later, and the lesson ends on a family prayer-list prompt.
ea-gh-ask-seek-knock.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Stuck waiting on an answer? Keep asking. Jesus' words in Matthew 7:7-8 carry the sense of continuing action: keep on asking, keep on seeking, keep on knocking. Every one that asks receives. You are not persuading a reluctant ruler; you are a child asking a good Father, and persistence is part of the way He set it up. Delay is not denial. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-ask-seek-knock.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Stuck waiting on an answer? Do not quit. Jesus told of the friend at midnight and the widow before the judge so that men ought always to pray and not to faint. Elijah sent his servant seven times before the cloud appeared, and Daniel learned his words were heard from the first day. So put your requests plainly before the Father, in His name and with thanksgiving, seek Him above His gifts, and keep knocking. His peace guards your heart while you wait, and every one that asks receives.

teen.open: Been praying for something and nothing's happened yet? Jesus says keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking. Waiting doesn't mean no.
teen.close: So don't give up. Keep bringing it to Yahweh like a kid asking a good dad. He hears you from the first day, and His peace holds you while you wait.

senior.open: The title asks what to do while waiting on an answer. Matthew 7:7-8 teaches a continuing posture: keep asking, keep seeking, keep knocking, for every one that asks receives.
senior.close: So waiting is no reason to stop. Persistence is part of how Jesus taught us to pray; delay is not denial, and the Father's peace keeps our hearts while His answer comes.

ea-gh-rock-house.reason: The first section answers it plainly (both heard and built; the doing is the foundation); the lesson ends on a hands-on rock-and-sand activity instead of the answer.
ea-gh-rock-house.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Two houses, one storm: what decides which one still stands? Doing what Jesus says. Both builders heard His sayings, both built, and both faced the same rain, floods and wind. The wise man heard and did; the foolish man heard and did not. The storm does not decide the outcome; it only reveals what each house was built on. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-rock-house.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What decides which house still stands when the rain comes? Not how much you heard, but whether you did it. Hearing alone deceives the hearer, like Ezekiel's listeners who enjoyed the sermon as a lovely song and went home unchanged. So dig deep now, while the weather is calm: take one thing you have heard and do it this week, in your money, marriage, ministry and parenting. Build out of love on Christ, the Rock. When the storm comes, as it will, your house falls not.

teen.open: Two houses, same storm. Why does one stand? Because that builder didn't just hear what Jesus said; he did it.
teen.close: So don't just listen to the Word. Pick one thing you've heard and actually do it this week. That's how you build on the Rock before the storm hits.

senior.open: The title asks what decides which house survives the storm. Jesus answers in Matthew 7:24-27: both men heard, but only the one who did His sayings built on the rock.
senior.close: So the foundation is laid by obedience, and it must be laid before the storm. Practised in love, day by day, the doing of the Word is what leaves us standing when the rain descends.

ea-gh-forgive-forgiven.reason: The first section states the answer (forgive and the Father forgives you; refuse and He will not), but the lesson ends on a family discussion prompt, not on the pipeline the title promised.
ea-gh-forgive-forgiven.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Matthew 6:14-15 say about the debts you refuse to release? It says your forgiveness runs through a pipeline. The mercy you extend to others is the same line the Father’s mercy flows to you through. Release the debt and the line is open; hold it and you clog your own supply. Here is how Jesus taught it.
ea-gh-forgive-forgiven.example: ONE NAME, ONE DEBT. Say a friend spread something false about you, and every time you pray the Lord’s Prayer the memory comes back. The lesson gives you the steps. Name the person. Name the debt. Tell the Father you release them, they owe you nothing, and you hand it to Him. You may still need time before trust is rebuilt; that is a separate thing. When the memory returns next week, you release it again.
ea-gh-forgive-forgiven.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does Matthew 6:14-15 say about the debts you refuse to release? That refusing to release them shuts off your own forgiveness supply. The king forgave ten thousand talents; the servant who would not forgive a hundred pence cut himself off from that mercy and served the sentence himself. So release the debt today, again and again if you must. Then the line to the Father stays clear, and you walk out of the prison you built.

teen.open: Jesus said the way you forgive others is tied to how the Father forgives you. Forgiveness is like a pipe: what you let flow out keeps the flow coming in.
teen.close: So what happens to a debt you will not release? It blocks your own line to the Father. Let it go today, and keep letting it go, and you walk free.

senior.open: The title calls forgiveness a pipeline, and Jesus taught exactly that. The mercy we extend to others is the channel through which we receive the Father’s mercy ourselves.
senior.close: So Matthew 6:14-15 answers plainly. A debt we refuse to release closes our own line of mercy. We were forgiven ten thousand talents; releasing the hundred pence others owe us keeps that line open and sets our own hearts free.

ea-gh-abide-fruit.reason: The plain answer (no: without Me ye can do nothing; the cut-off branch withers) is stated in sections three and eight; the opening implies it and the lesson ends on a discussion prompt.
ea-gh-abide-fruit.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you unplug from the Source and still bear fruit? No. Jesus said without Him we can do nothing, not a little less but nothing. A branch bears grapes by staying connected to the vine, not by straining, and a branch cut off withers. Abiding means staying in Him every day, with His Word in you, prayer going up and obedience flowing out. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-abide-fruit.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you unplug from the Source and still bear fruit? No. The branch cut off may look green for a little while, but it has no life of its own. Fruit is a connection metric, not an effort metric. Stay in the Vine: keep His Word in you, pray, obey, accept the Father’s pruning. Then the fruit takes care of itself: love, joy, peace, lives touched, prayers that land, and fruit that remains.

teen.open: Can you cut yourself off from Jesus and still grow good fruit? No. He said without Him you can do nothing. A branch grows by staying on the vine.
teen.close: So the answer is no, you cannot unplug and still bear fruit. Stay close: read His Word, talk to Him, obey Him. The fruit grows from that.

senior.open: The title asks whether a life cut off from its Source can still bear fruit. Jesus answers plainly that it cannot: without Him we can do nothing, and the fruit comes from abiding, not from effort.
senior.close: So the answer stands. No branch bears fruit of itself. The one who stays in Him, with His Word abiding within, prayer rising and obedience following, bears fruit that remains, even in old age.

ea-gh-believe-life.reason: The first section names both sides (He gave His Son; we believe on Him), but the turn that is yours is spread through later sections and the lesson ends on a discussion prompt.
ea-gh-believe-life.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What is already given, and what is still in your hands? Yahweh so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, and on the cross the rescue was finished. Nothing remains to be added. What remains is your turn: to look to the Son, believe on Him and receive Him. Whoever does has everlasting life, starting now. Here is how John 3:16 shows it.
ea-gh-believe-life.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What is the gift already given, and what is the choice still in your hands? The gift is the Son, given in love while we were still sinners, and the rescue He finished on the cross. The choice is yours: look to Him the way Israel looked to the serpent on the pole, believe on Him, receive Him, and follow Him home. Whoever believes is not condemned. He has passed from death unto life, and the life never ends.

teen.open: Yahweh already gave the biggest gift: His Son. The rescue is done. Your part is to believe on Jesus and receive Him.
teen.close: So what is left for you? Not earning it. Just your turn to believe on Jesus, receive Him, and follow Him. That life starts now and never ends.

senior.open: John 3:16 sets out both sides of the rescue. Yahweh gave His only begotten Son and the work is finished; what remains in our hands is to believe on Him and receive the gift.
senior.close: So the plan is plain. The giving and the rescuing are done; the receiving is our choice. Whoever believes on the Son has everlasting life now, knowing the Father and the Son, and is held in a hand no one can pluck him from.

ea-gh-stand-on-word.reason: The opening section ends on the answer (he looked at the wind instead of the Word and the footing went), but the lesson closes on a discussion prompt after many side sections.
ea-gh-stand-on-word.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Peter sink the moment he looks away? Because the footing was never his. He walked on the water by standing on one word from Jesus: Come. While his eyes held the One who spoke it, the water held him. When he looked at the wind and then at himself, the threat grew bigger and the footing went. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-stand-on-word.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does Peter sink the moment he looks away? Because he took his eyes off the One whose Word was holding him up and put them on the wind and on himself. Self-focus under threat makes the threat look bigger. So keep your eyes on Jesus, stand your full weight on what He said, and let Him increase. And if you do sink, cry out, Lord, save me. His hand is already there.

teen.open: Peter walked on water because Jesus said, Come. He sank when he stopped looking at Jesus and looked at the wind instead.
teen.close: So why did Peter sink? He looked away from Jesus. Keep your eyes on Him and stand on what He says. And if you start to sink, call out. He will catch you.

senior.open: Peter did not walk on the water by his own strength. He stood on the word of Jesus, and he sank when his attention moved from that Word to the wind and to himself.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Peter sank because he looked away from the footing that was never his own. We stand when our eyes stay on Jesus and our weight rests on His Word, and when we falter, His hand is quick to catch us.

ea-gh-grain-wheat.reason: The first section answers plainly (a seed kept safe stays single; buried, it brings forth much fruit), but the lesson ends on a seed-in-a-cup discussion prompt rather than the harvest.
ea-gh-grain-wheat.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What happens when you finally stop guarding your seed? It falls into the ground, dies to its present form, and brings forth much fruit. A seed kept safe in a jar stays a single seed forever. Jesus was the first Grain, buried and raised, and every gift Yahweh gives you works the same way. Here is how John 12:24 shows it.
ea-gh-grain-wheat.example: A GIFT IN A JAR. Say someone has a gift for teaching children and keeps it to himself because he is afraid of doing it badly. Kept that way, it stays one talent, exactly as it was, like the servant who hid his in the earth. If he plants it, by teaching a class, the gift is poured out into others. He cannot make it grow by staring at it. His part is the planting; Yahweh gives the increase.
ea-gh-grain-wheat.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What happens when you finally stop guarding your seed? The harvest begins. A gift kept safe stays singular; a gift that is really buried, in service, in generosity, in sharing, comes up as much fruit you could not have imagined. There may be a dark season and tears between the sowing and the reaping, but those who sow in tears reap in joy. Plant it, trust Yahweh with the increase, and look for the harvest on the far side of the burial.

teen.open: A seed kept in a jar stays one seed. A seed planted in the ground dies and grows into a harvest. That is what happens when you stop guarding what Yahweh gave you.
teen.close: So what happens when you stop guarding your seed? It grows. Plant your gifts by using them for others, trust Yahweh to grow them, and the harvest comes.

senior.open: Jesus answered this with a grain of wheat. Kept safe, it abides alone; let fall into the ground to die, it brings forth much fruit. The same holds for every gift He gives us.
senior.close: So the answer is a harvest. What we stop protecting and truly plant, our gifts, our means, our very selves, Yahweh multiplies. The sowing may come with tears, but the one who sows in tears comes again rejoicing, bringing his sheaves.

ea-gh-closet.reason: The title claims the hidden room shapes the public life, but that link (the public life is funded by the private one) only arrives in the next-to-last section; the start is the Matthew 6 setting.
ea-gh-closet.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How does your hidden prayer room shape your public life? In Matthew 6:6 Jesus says to go into an inner room, shut the door, and pray to your Father with no one watching. There, with no audience to perform for, the real you shows up, and He teaches you. Then He rewards you openly: what you learn in secret shows up in public. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-closet.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How does your hidden prayer room shape your public life? It funds it. Every audience bends us toward performance, so the closed door is the one place the unedited self meets the Father and is taught. Jesus kept that room before the crowds; Daniel kept it long before the lions. What is formed there, wisdom, steadiness, peace under pressure, love that needs no applause, is what shows up in the open, rewarded in His time.

teen.open: Jesus said to pray alone with the door shut, where no one is watching. What happens there shapes who you are in front of everyone else.
teen.close: So how does secret prayer shape your public life? It is where Yahweh teaches the real you. What He builds there shows up later, out in the open.

senior.open: Jesus taught that the most important prayer happens behind a closed door, with no audience. The Father who sees in secret teaches us there, and He rewards that hidden life openly.
senior.close: So the answer is that the public life is funded by the private one. As Daniel’s habit held when the crisis came, what Yahweh teaches us in secret becomes the steadiness and wisdom others later see.

ea-gh-feed-sheep.reason: The answer (faithful people you teach, who will teach others, per 2 Timothy 2:2) is reasoned out in section three, after the shore scene; the lesson ends on a discussion prompt.
ea-gh-feed-sheep.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who gets your deposit when you are gone? The faithful people you pour the Word into, who will be able to teach others also. Jesus asked Peter three times if he loved Him and each time answered, feed My sheep. Paul handed the same deposit to Timothy to pass to faithful men. Love for Jesus shows up as feeding His sheep, and that chain keeps going after you. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-feed-sheep.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who gets your deposit when you are gone? The ones you feed, and the ones they feed after them. Paul, Timothy, faithful men, others also: four generations in one verse. Jesus invested in twelve, and it is still compounding. You did not design this deposit; you pass on the same Word that was given to you. Feed His sheep, teach people who can teach, and the Word keeps multiplying in generations you will never meet.

teen.open: When you are gone, who has what you learned about Jesus? The people you taught. Jesus told Peter, if you love Me, feed My sheep.
teen.close: So who gets your deposit? The people you share Jesus with, and the people they share Him with next. Pick someone to pour into this year.

senior.open: The question is who carries on what we were given. Jesus answered it on the shore with Peter: love Him by feeding His sheep. Paul answered it to Timothy: commit it to faithful men who will teach others also.
senior.close: So the deposit goes to those we teach and to those they teach after them. We honor the ones who poured into us by pouring into others, and the same Word keeps multiplying long after we are gone.

ea-gh-filled-righteousness.reason: The tie between the hunger, the cost and a Kingdom that cannot be repossessed is only made in the final sections (Table in the Wilderness, Happy Under Fire); it ends on a discussion prompt.
ea-gh-filled-righteousness.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does Matthew 5 tie your deepest hunger to a Kingdom that cannot be taken back? Because Jesus blesses those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, rightness with Yahweh and right living before Him, and promises they shall be filled. That same hunger will cost you, and to those persecuted for it He promises the Kingdom of heaven. Hunger and cost come together, and so do the filling and the Kingdom. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-filled-righteousness.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does Matthew 5 tie your deepest hunger to a Kingdom that cannot be taken back? Because the hunger for righteousness that fills you is the same hunger that draws fire, and the Kingdom is attached to both. Aim your appetite at the Word and at Jesus, the Bread of life. Make sure you suffer for well doing, not foolishness. Then you are filled, the Kingdom is yours, and your happiness cannot be repossessed, because it never came from the approval of those who oppose you.

teen.open: Jesus said people who are hungry to do right will be filled. Doing right will cost you sometimes, and He promised those people the Kingdom.
teen.close: So why tie your hunger to the Kingdom? Because wanting what is right fills you and also costs you, and the Kingdom comes with both. No one can take that away from you.

senior.open: Jesus placed two blessings side by side: the hungry for righteousness shall be filled, and the persecuted for righteousness shall have the Kingdom. The hunger and its cost belong together.
senior.close: So the answer is that the right hunger and its cost lead to the same reward. When we seek righteousness and suffer for well doing, we are filled, the Kingdom is ours, and that joy cannot be repossessed by anyone.

ea-gh-sheep-voice.reason: The answer (belonging comes first, and an ear saturated in His Word knows a stranger’s voice before the mind finishes arguing) sits in sections three and five; it ends on a discussion prompt.
ea-gh-sheep-voice.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Could you hear a stranger’s voice before you follow it? Yes, if you belong to the Shepherd and know His voice well. Jesus said His sheep will not follow a stranger but flee, because they know not the voice of strangers. They do not need to argue down every false voice. An ear filled with the true Voice simply hears that the other one is wrong. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-sheep-voice.example: THE OFF-KEY VOICE. Say you scroll a feed at night and a stream of posts tells you to be afraid of everything and angry at everyone. You have not memorized an answer to each one. But you have been reading the Word every morning, and these voices do not sound like the Shepherd. So you do not stay to argue with them. Like a sheep at the gate, you turn away and follow the Voice you know.
ea-gh-sheep-voice.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Could you hear a stranger’s voice before you follow it? You can, because belonging trains the ear. Chosen in Him and given His Spirit, the sheep come to know the Shepherd’s voice, and recognition beats analysis. Samuel learned the voice; so do we, by reason of use. Saturate yourself in His Word until it is familiar, answer like Samuel, speak, for thy servant heareth, and the counterfeit will register as strange before it can lead you anywhere.

teen.open: Can you tell a fake voice before you follow it? Yes, if you know Jesus’ voice well. His sheep know Him, and a stranger’s voice just sounds wrong.
teen.close: So yes, you can spot the fake. Spend time in His Word until His voice is familiar. Then the wrong voices sound off, and you do not have to follow them.

senior.open: Jesus taught that His sheep will not follow a stranger, because they do not know the stranger’s voice. The ability to spot a counterfeit grows out of belonging to the Shepherd and knowing Him well.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. An ear long trained in the Word recognizes a false voice before the argument is finished. Like Samuel, we learn His voice by reason of use, and we rest in knowing no one can pluck us from His hand.

ea-gh-word-framed-worlds.reason: Section two states the answer outright (reality is authored, not accidental; framed by His Word), but the lesson ends on a family discussion prompt rather than landing the Author and His design.
ea-gh-word-framed-worlds.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Is reality an accident or an authored design? It is authored. John, Hebrews and Colossians agree: the worlds were framed by the Word, fitted together to a plan, and all things were made by Him and for Him. He stands before all things and outside them, and by Him all things hold together. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-word-framed-worlds.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Is reality an accident or an authored design? An authored design. The Word who was in the beginning framed the worlds, spoke and it was done, upholds all things now, and was made flesh and dwelt among us. That changes how you live. Read the Scriptures as the Author’s own account of what He made. Let His intent outrank the system’s defaults. See the design, name the Designer, and give Him the honor it is all pointing toward.

teen.open: Did everything just happen by accident? No. The Bible says the world was designed and made by the Word, Jesus, who was there before anything else.
teen.close: So reality is not an accident. It was made on purpose by Jesus, the Word, and it is held together by Him. Live like you belong to the One who made it all.

senior.open: John 1, Hebrews 11 and Colossians 1 answer this together. The worlds were framed by the Word of Yahweh; all things were made by Him and for Him, and He stands before all things.
senior.close: So reality is an authored design, not an accident. The One who framed the worlds speaks to us in the Scriptures, and a life ordered under His purpose is a life lived inside the true frame, creature to Creator.

ea-gh-appointment-kept.reason: Opens with the full Luke 2 passage; how Simeon and Anna came to be there (not luck but positioning: they kept the posture, He kept the clock) is only stated near the end.
ea-gh-appointment-kept.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. How were Simeon and Anna in the right place at the exact moment promised? Not by luck. Simeon was just and devout, the Holy Ghost was upon him, and he came by the Spirit into the temple. Anna had served there with fasting and prayer for decades. They kept a ready posture, and Yahweh kept the clock. Here is how Luke shows it.
ea-gh-appointment-kept.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. How were Simeon and Anna standing in the right place at the exact moment promised? They were positioned, not lucky. One followed a specific word from the Holy Ghost; the other kept a lifetime of faithful presence. Both waited in the Spirit, and on the very day the Child was brought in, Yahweh supplied the timing. So set your clock to His: stay where He leads, in the Word, in prayer and in worship, and trust Him to bring you to every appointment He has promised.

teen.open: Simeon and Anna were in the temple at the exact moment baby Jesus arrived. It was not luck. They had been waiting faithfully, and Yahweh brought the moment to them.
teen.close: So how were they in the right place? They kept showing up and listening to the Holy Spirit, and Yahweh did the timing. You can do the same.

senior.open: Simeon and Anna met the promised Christ on the very day He was presented. Luke shows this was no accident: they kept a faithful posture, and Yahweh kept the appointed time.
senior.close: So the answer is positioning, not luck. They waited in the Spirit and stayed where they were led, even in old age, and the One who keeps His clock brought the promise to them at the very hour.

ea-gh-no-guile-figtree.reason: The title’s point (He knows you before you speak, so pretense has nothing to work with, and being known and still received ends hiding) arrives in sections five and seven.
ea-gh-no-guile-figtree.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What does Jesus seeing Nathanael under the fig tree change about pretending? It ends the point of it. Jesus knew Nathanael’s heart before he said a word, and He knows yours the same way. You cannot impress Him with a performance or fool Him with a mask. And He saw Nathanael to draw him close, not to shame him. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-no-guile-figtree.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does what Jesus saw under the fig tree change about pretending? Everything. Before Philip called him, Nathanael was already seen, and named honestly as a man with no guile. Pretense has nothing to work with when all things are open before Him. But being fully known and still received is the opposite of shame. So come and see, as you really are. Bring your honest doubts and your real self. You are already known, and you are still welcome.

teen.open: Jesus knew all about Nathanael before they ever met. He knows you the same way, so there is no point pretending with Him.
teen.close: So what changes? You can stop pretending. Jesus already sees the real you, and He still calls you close. Come to Him just as you are.

senior.open: Jesus told Nathanael He had seen him under the fig tree before they met. The One we come to already knows the heart, so pretense has nothing to work with.
senior.close: So the answer is freedom from the mask. We are known before we speak, and still received. That is the one condition under which a person can finally stop hiding and worship honestly.

teen.close: So you are known and still responsible. Peter and Judas both failed. Peter ran back to Jesus. When you mess up, run toward Him, not away.

teen.close: So did that thought start with you? Check it. Notice it, test it with the Word, and if it fails, refuse it and think on something true instead.

senior.close: So the answer is that a thought may not be ours, and we need not sign for it. We notice it, test it against Philippians 4:8, take it captive if it fails, and turn the mind to what is true, kept in His peace.

ea-gh-spirits-seek-a-body.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Swept clean but still empty? Then the house is not safe yet. The man in Matthew 12 was delivered, but nothing moved in, and he ended worse than before. You are not your own; you were bought with a price, and the Father and the Son make Their abode with those who love Him. So when you remove something harmful, put something holy in its place. Be filled with the Spirit, let the Word dwell in you richly, and the Owner in residence leaves no room for the return.

teen.open: Jesus told about a house that was cleaned out but left empty, and something worse moved in. Quitting a bad thing is not enough. Your life needs Jesus living in it.
teen.close: So is clean but empty good enough? No. When you stop something bad, fill that space with something good, and ask the Holy Spirit to fill you every day.

senior.open: Matthew 12 warns that a house swept clean but left empty invites a worse return. Removing evil is only half the work; the house needs its rightful Owner living there.
senior.close: So the answer is to be filled, not merely emptied. Our bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit. When we replace what is harmful with the Word, worship and good works, we give no place to the enemy.

ea-gh-not-my-will-but-thine.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you pray not my will and still feel safe? You can, because the will you are yielding to belongs to a faithful Creator who wills your soul to prosper. Jesus prayed both halves, the honest request and the surrender, and then committed His spirit into the Father’s hands. Do the same. Tell Him what you want, place it beneath His word, keep doing good, and rest. What you commit to Him, He is able to keep against that day.

teen.open: Jesus prayed, not My will but Yours, on the hardest night of His life. You can pray that too and still feel safe, because the Father is faithful.
teen.close: So can you give Him your will and still be safe? Yes. Tell Him honestly what you want, then trust Him with it. He takes good care of what you give Him.

senior.open: Jesus prayed not my will but Thine in Gethsemane, and Peter calls suffering believers to commit their souls to a faithful Creator. The safety of surrender rests on the One who receives it.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. Surrender is not loss but a deposit placed with a faithful Creator who wills our souls to prosper. We pray honestly, yield to His will, keep doing good, and rest in His keeping.

ea-gh-wheat-and-tares.reason: The answer (not always: tares look like wheat and roots tangle; discern fruit, but the final sorting is the angels’ at the harvest, not yours) arrives in sections three to five.
ea-gh-wheat-and-tares.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you tell wheat from weeds? Not always, and you do not have to. ea-gh-wheat-and-tares.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you tell wheat from weeds? Sometimes you can see the fruit, and you should discern it. teen.open: In Jesus’ story, weeds grow right next to wheat and look a lot like it. You cannot always tell them apart, and sorting them is not your job.
teen.close: So can you tell wheat from weeds? Not always. Notice how people act, but leave the final judging to Jesus. Your job is to grow as good wheat.

senior.open: The parable of the tares teaches that the good and the false grow together in this world, often hard to tell apart. Discerning fruit is ours; the final harvest of souls is His.
senior.close: So we may discern fruit, but we are not the reapers. The harvest is certain and belongs to Him. Our calling is to live as visible wheat, patient and fruitful, until the righteous shine forth as the sun.

ea-gh-sheep-and-goats.example: A CUP OF COLD WATER. Say an older neighbor on your street has been sick for weeks and no one visits. You are not trying to earn anything. You belong to the Shepherd, so you bring a meal, sit with him for an hour, and come back next week. You may never think of it again. But the King said that whatever is done for one of the least of these His brethren is done to Him.
ea-gh-sheep-and-goats.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What does the Shepherd’s division mean for today’s choices? It means the growing-together will end, and the choices you make now show whose you are. There is no third pen. Kindness does not buy a place at His right hand; salvation is a gift. But those who belong to the Shepherd hear His voice and love the people He loves, often without keeping score. So follow Him here, feed the hungry, welcome the stranger, visit the sick, and the separation there holds no fear.

teen.open: Jesus said a day is coming when He will separate people like a shepherd separates sheep from goats. That means what you choose today really matters.
teen.close: So what does it mean for today? Follow Jesus now, and show it by helping people who need it. Those small choices show whose you are.

senior.open: Matthew 25 shows the King separating the nations as a shepherd divides sheep from goats. Because that separation is real and final, the choices of this present life carry great weight.
senior.close: So the division answers how we should live today. We rest in grace, follow the Shepherd’s voice, and let that belonging show in care for the least of His brethren, so that day holds no fear for us.

ea-gh-judgment-committed-to-son.reason: The first section states it outright (the Father has committed all judgment unto the Son), but the lesson ends on a discussion prompt instead of landing why that is good news.

ea-gh-judgment-committed-to-son.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who holds the gavel over every soul? The Son, by the Father’s own appointment. That settles two things. First, the Judge is not a faceless power; He has a face and a Name, His judgment is just, and He came first to save. Second, the seat of judging souls is not yours. You give account for yourself, not for everyone else. So honour the Son as the Father, leave every soul’s case with Him, and live toward His seat with confidence, because the Judge loved you first.

teen.open: Who decides the final judgment for every person? Jesus. The Father gave all judgment to the Son, and He is the One who died for us.
teen.close: So who holds the gavel? Jesus does, not you. That means you can stop judging other people’s hearts and trust the Judge who loves you.

senior.open: Jesus said in John 5 that the Father judges no man but has committed all judgment unto the Son. The One who will judge every soul is the Son of man Himself.
senior.close: So the gavel belongs to the Son. That removes the dread of a faceless judgment and the burden of judging others ourselves. We honour Him as we honour the Father and give account only for our own lives.

ea-gh-hear-believe-no-condemnation.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Already passed over? If you hear His word and believe on the One who sent Him, yes. teen.open: Jesus said if you hear His word and believe, you already have everlasting life and you have passed from death to life. That is now, not someday.
teen.close: So are you already passed over? If you believe, yes. Jesus took the punishment. Live thankful, not scared, and show it by loving people.

senior.open: John 5:24 is the Judge publishing His verdict in advance. The one who hears His word and believes on the Father has everlasting life now and shall not come into condemnation.
senior.close: So the answer is yes, for all who hear and believe. The verdict rests on the sentence Christ already bore. We may live in full assurance, without terror, letting love for others show that we have passed from death unto life.

senior.close: So the Word that will measure us is the Word offered to us now, in mercy. We are given years to know, love and live it, and to share it with those we love before that day.

teen.open: Yes, someone is trying to steal who you are. Jesus said the thief comes to steal, and he goes after the truth that Yahweh made you in His image.
teen.close: So is someone trying to rob your identity? Yes. When lies about who you are show up, call them out and answer with what the Word says about you.

senior.close: So the answer is yes, but the theft can be refused. We recognize lies about our worth as robbery, answer them with what is written, and give the glory back to the Maker, held safe in the Good Shepherd’s hand.

teen.open: Does Yahweh ever try to make you sin? No. When we pray lead us not into temptation, we are asking Him to guard us, and then we stay alert.
teen.close: So is temptation from Yahweh? Never. Ask Him to guard you, watch out for your weak spots, and when you need to run from something, run.

senior.open: Scripture is plain that Yahweh tempts no one. The petition lead us not into temptation is a request for His guard, and it is kept by our own sober watchfulness.
senior.close: So temptation is never His doing. We ask the faithful Keeper to guard us, and we watch: guarding our desires, avoiding the path of evil, and fleeing when we must, resting in the One who never sleeps.

senior.close: So Philip’s question is a caution for us. Familiarity is not understanding. The Father is seen in the face of Jesus, and we keep asking the Spirit to turn our nearness into true sight.

ea-gh-he-already-knew.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did Jesus really need Philip’s answer? Not at all. teen.close: So did Jesus need Philip’s answer? No. He already had the plan. When you face something impossible, trust Him instead of just doing the math.

senior.open: John tells us Jesus asked Philip about bread to prove him, for He already knew what He would do. The question was for Philip’s growth, not for Jesus’ information.
senior.close: So Jesus did not need the answer; Philip needed the question. When Yahweh sets an impossible need before us, He already holds the answer, and the right response is faith rather than fearful calculation.

Now a friend at church has just been laid off. The comfort you received is the very comfort you can pass on. You call him, sit with him, pray with him, and tell him honestly what helped. Your hard season is now strength for someone else.
ea-gh-strengthen-your-brethren.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who are you pulling up? Whoever is now where you once were. teen.open: Jesus told Peter that after he came through his hard test, he should help others. What you learn in hard times is meant to help someone else.
teen.close: So who are you pulling up? Someone going through what you already went through. Find them and help them up, like Jesus did for Peter.

senior.open: Jesus told Peter that once he was converted he should strengthen his brethren. The growth that comes through testing is given to be spent on others, not kept.
senior.close: So the answer is those who now stand where we once stood. As Peter was restored and became a strengthener, our own trials prepare us to comfort, support and lift the next generation.

ea-gh-glory-refused-or-taken.reason: Herod and Nebuchadnezzar show the outcome early, but who gets the applause (receive honest thanks, hand the glory up to Yahweh, built as a reflex) is stated only in the closing sections.
ea-gh-glory-refused-or-taken.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Who gets the applause you earned? You may receive honest thanks between people, but the glory goes up to Yahweh. When the crowd called Herod a god, he let it stick, and he was struck down. Nebuchadnezzar boasted of what he built by his own might, and he was driven out until he praised the King of heaven. Glory that lands on the wrong person brings it down. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-glory-refused-or-taken.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Who gets the applause you earned? You can receive the honest thanks; the glory you hand up. That is not self-deprecation, which would be false, but redirection, which is obedience. Herod and Nebuchadnezzar let glory stick and fell. The angel, Paul, Barnabas and Peter refused it instantly, because the reflex was built before the moment. So build it now, in ordinary weeks, every time a meal or a project or a compliment goes well. Then glory passes through you instead of sticking, and your gifts are safe to hold.

teen.open: When people praise you, who should get the glory? You can say thank you, but the glory belongs to Yahweh. Herod kept it for himself, and it destroyed him.
teen.close: So who gets the applause? Say thanks, then point the glory up to Yahweh. Practice it on small things now, so it is easy when big praise comes.

senior.open: Herod and Nebuchadnezzar let glory that belonged to Yahweh rest on themselves, and both were brought low. The applause we earn may be thanked, but the glory must be passed upward.
senior.close: So the answer is redirection. We accept honest thanks, refuse the worship we were never owed, and give the glory to Yahweh. A reflex built in ordinary days keeps success from becoming our ruin.

ea-gh-before-abraham-i-am.reason: Section two answers plainly (not I was but I AM: He took the Name given to Moses at the bush), but the lesson ends on a discussion prompt rather than landing the claim.
ea-gh-before-abraham-i-am.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. What did Jesus mean by saying I AM in John 8:58? He did not say before Abraham was, I was. He took the present-tense Name Yahweh gave Moses at the burning bush, I AM THAT I AM, and applied it to Himself. He was not claiming to be very old; He was claiming to be the One who simply is. His hearers understood and picked up stones. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-before-abraham-i-am.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. What did Jesus mean by I AM? He meant that the One who gave the Name to Moses was standing in the temple courts in a human body, wearing it. The crowd reached for stones; the high priest heard the same two words at His trial; Thomas answered rightly after the resurrection. A good teacher does not claim the Name, so the middle option is closed. Meet Him as the Eternal Son of Yahweh, worship Him, and trust His promises, for they are as secure as the Name itself.

teen.open: When Jesus said, before Abraham was, I am, He used the name Yahweh gave Moses at the burning bush. He was saying He is Yahweh, who always is.
teen.close: So what did Jesus mean? He was saying He is the I AM, the One who always was and always is. That is why we worship Him, not just admire Him.

senior.open: Jesus did not say before Abraham was, I was. He said I am, taking the Name revealed to Moses at the bush. His hearers understood the claim and took up stones.
senior.close: So Jesus meant that He is the I AM, the eternal One who existed before Abraham and before the world. That claim leaves no room for a merely good teacher; it calls for worship and gives His promises their certainty.

ea-gh-name-that-saves.reason: Opens on Joseph's dream; the name's meaning (Yahweh saves) arrives in section two, and what calling on Him today means only surfaces in the last two sections before a family-talk ending.
ea-gh-name-that-saves.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why does the name JESUS already carry its rescue? Because the name is the Hebrew Yeshua, Joshua, which means Yahweh saves, and the angel gave it before He was born with the reason attached: He shall save His people from their sins. And calling on Him today means confessing Him as Lord and believing Yahweh raised Him, praying in His name, and adding nothing of your own. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-name-that-saves.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why does the name JESUS already carry its rescue? Because the name was the work, stated in advance and then performed: announced to Joseph and Mary, given on the eighth day, and finished at the cross, where His blood cleanses from all sin. There is none other name whereby we must be saved (Acts 4:12). So to call on Him today is simple: confess Him, believe Yahweh raised Him, and pray in His name. Every time you say Jesus, you are saying Yahweh saves, and He does.

teen.open: Why does the name Jesus carry a rescue inside it? Because Jesus means Yahweh saves, and the angel gave the name before He was born: He shall save His people from their sins.
teen.close: So the name says what He does. Jesus means Yahweh saves, and He finished that work at the cross. Calling on Him today means believing in Him, saying He is Lord, and praying in His name. Nothing else needs adding.

senior.open: The title asks why the name Jesus already carries its rescue. The answer is in the name itself: it means Yahweh saves, and it was given before His birth with the reason attached, that He would save His people from their sins.
senior.close: So the question has a plain answer. The name was the work, announced before and finished at the cross. To call on Him today is to confess Him as Lord, believe Yahweh raised Him, and pray in His name, trusting His mercy rather than our merit.

ea-gh-all-power-is-his.reason: The answer (authority is issued, not generated; you stand in His power) is stated in section three and pictured by the centurion and officer; the opening is narration and the end is a family-talk prompt.
ea-gh-all-power-is-his.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Do you have to build your own power? No. Jesus said all power in heaven and earth is given to Him, and then He gave His people power over all the power of the enemy (Luke 10:19). Authority in a believer is issued, never generated. That changes how you stand: not straining to be strong enough, but standing quietly in His name, the way a man under authority does. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-all-power-is-his.example: TWO WAYS TO FACE ONE TEMPTATION. Say a believer is hit by the same temptation two nights in a row. The first night she tries to work herself up, louder and more intense, and ends up anxious and afraid she did not pray hard enough. The second night she remembers she is under authority. She speaks His name quietly, asks in His name, and stands. Same temptation, same believer. The difference is where she thinks the power comes from.
ea-gh-all-power-is-his.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Do you have to build your own power? No, and trying to only produces fear in the moment that calls for calm. All power belongs to Jesus, and He hands it to those He sends, like a centurion's orders backed by the one above him. You are complete in Him, with nothing to add. So in prayer, in temptation and in daily obedience, you stop striving and stand in His name, quietly and confidently, rejoicing most that your name is written in heaven.

teen.open: Do you have to make yourself strong enough for Yahweh to use you? No. Jesus has all power, and He gives His people authority to stand in His name.
teen.close: So you do not have to build your own power. It is given, not made. Stand in Jesus' name calmly, like an officer backed by the law, and remember the best part: your name is written in heaven.

senior.open: The title says you do not have to build your own power, and the lesson shows why. All power is given to Jesus in heaven and earth, and the authority a believer carries is issued by Him, never generated by our own intensity.
senior.close: So the answer stands. Authority is something we stand in, not something we build. Like the centurion, we are under authority, and that is why we can be calm. We are complete in Him, and our deepest joy is not the power but belonging to the One who holds it.

ea-gh-without-me-nothing.reason: John 15 is laid out first; the plain answer (a branch produces nothing it did not receive, so fruit comes from abiding) is spread across sections and only gathered in WHAT CHANGES before the talk prompt.
ea-gh-without-me-nothing.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Why is staying connected the real source of lasting fruit? Because a branch produces nothing it did not receive. The fruit comes from the vine, not from the branch's effort, so fruit is evidence of connection, never of the branch. Jesus said it plainly: apart from Him we can do nothing (John 15:5). Chasing fruit somewhere else only cuts you off from what made you fruitful. Here is how the Word shows it.
ea-gh-without-me-nothing.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why is staying connected the real source of lasting fruit? Because the power is in the Vine. Even the Son did nothing of Himself, and the branch that detaches withers no matter how fruitful it once was. Abiding is a relationship kept day after day: His words living in you, prayer, obedience and love, sitting at His feet like Mary. Keep that connection, and the fruit follows, fruit that remains, even in old age, even through pruning.

teen.open: Where does real, lasting fruit in your life come from? Not from trying harder somewhere else. A branch only bears fruit by staying connected to the vine, and Jesus is the Vine.
teen.close: So stop chasing fruit on your own. Stay connected to Jesus through His Word, prayer, obeying Him and loving others. When you abide, the fruit comes, and it lasts.

senior.open: The title asks why staying connected to Him is the real source of lasting output. The lesson's answer is that a branch produces nothing it did not receive; fruit is the evidence of connection, never of the branch's own effort.
senior.close: So the answer is settled. Lasting fruit comes from abiding, not striving. Measure your life by connection rather than output, keep His words, prayer, obedience and love at the centre, and trust the Vinedresser in dry seasons. The psalm promises fruit even in old age.
